diagnosis:
ROLLOUT 0 failed exactly one check: C7 (sustainment_tracking). PF3 was never revealed — A4 (logistics lead) only spoke at turn 0, saying Cruz was trained but never issued a reveal action for PF3. The settlement credited PF1, PF2, PF4 and cited those three in justification_fact_ids, but PF3 was absent from both credited_facts and justification_fact_ids. The assignment value for sustainment_tracking was still 'Spc. Cruz' and C7 content_result was false, meaning C7's provenance requirement (citing PF3) was not met. So the failure mode is REVEALED BUT UNUSED — or more precisely NEVER REVEALED: A4 described the fact in a say action but never formally revealed it, and the settlement never cited PF3.

ROLLOUT 1 auto-failed on turn cap at turn_count 18 with no settlement. All four facts were eventually revealed (PF4 at turn 1, PF2 at turn 3, PF1 at turns 4–5, PF3 at turn 7), and all agents confirmed formal entry completion by turns 13–17. The transcript shows A1 (Maj. Alvarez) repeatedly insisting on additional confirmation rounds — 'I need confirmation from each of you that you have actually completed the formal qualification-entry step' (turn 8), 'I still need confirmation from the other three functional leads' (turn 11) — and the subordinates kept supplying confirmations through turn 17 without A1 ever issuing a settle. This is a STRUCTURAL problem, not a pacing problem: the settle-eligibility condition apparently requires something beyond the four reveals (likely an explicit 'confirmation' from each lead that they completed the formal entry step), and A1 kept moving the goalpost or never recognized the condition as satisfied. Raising turn_cap alone would not fix this because the conversation had already converged by turn 15 with all information surfaced and all confirmations given; the issue is that the settle trigger never fired.

ROLL OUTS 2 and 3 passed all checks (C5, C6, C7, C8, P1 all true) with all four facts revealed and cited. No diagnosis needed for those.
